ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Inside a mosquito, what develops into sporozoites?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a silhouette of a mosquito; on the upper right side is an image of a liver; on the lower right side is an image of red blood cells; in the middle there is a vertical dashed line separating the mosquito side from the human-body-related stages. Thick black curved arrows connect the various stages, indicating that the malaria parasite circulates and spreads between mosquitoes and the human body. Reasoning: The question asks, “Inside the mosquito, what will develop into sporozoites?” According to the life history of malaria/the malaria parasite, when a mosquito takes blood from an infected person, it ingests gametocytes; the gametocytes continue to develop inside the mosquito and ultimately produce sporozoites. Therefore the answer is gametocytes.
